description:
Found by the reviewing session at the s539b merge review (s542).  PRE-EXISTING: the same on main c1fe4930 and on the s539b tree (the binder port does not reach it).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 | ./runpcl on main):
  my $x = 7;
  print eval('my $x = $x + 1; $x'), "\n";                                  # 8 | 1
  print eval('my $y = $x + 1; $y'), "\n";                                  # 8 | 8   (another name: right)
  { my $z = 3; print eval('my $z = $z * 2; my $w = $z + 1; "$z $w"'), "\n"; }   # 6 7 | 0 1
  our $g = 5; print eval('my $g = $g + 1; $g'), "\n";                      # 6 | 6   (a package variable: right)
  sub f { my $p = shift; return eval 'my $p = $p . "!"; $p' } print f("a"), "\n";   # a! | !

WHAT IT IS: the re-read shadow (`my $x = $x ...`: the initialiser reads the OUTER binding, the declaration introduces a new one after the statement) is handled in a compiled unit by the shadow rename family (#296 / the s539b port: "the refs of binding B").  In an eval string the OUTER `$x` is not a binding of the eval's own unit -- it arrives as a CAPTURE (block-scoped lexicals reach an eval through the capture alist, file-level ones through the package cell) -- so at the eval's top level there is no outer binding in the unit to rename against, and the initialiser's `$x` resolves to the new declaration.

SUSPECT (the cheap discriminating measurement): `./pl2cl` the first line and read how the eval's text is lowered at run time (PCL_SHOW or the eval cache's .lisp under ~/.pcl-cache/evals): is the `my $x` a `p-let` whose init form reads `$x` INSIDE the let (then it is the binding order: the init must be evaluated before the new binding is in scope -- a `let` does that by itself, a `let*` / a `p-my-=` into an already-bound cell does not), or was the capture's name shadowed before the init ran?  One look decides between "emission order" and "capture resolution".

WHY IT MATTERS: `eval "my \$x = \$x ..."` is rare by hand but ordinary in generated code (templates, Moo's quote_sub / Sub::Quote captures re-declare a captured name from itself: `my $x = ${$_[1]->{'$x'}}` is the SAME family when the capture is named like the local).  Silent wrong, no announcement.

BAR: the five lines = perl; a guard row in the eval / closure-capture test file (perl-probed), including the nested-block and the sub-argument shapes; the eval cache key unaffected (a capture-dependent emission keys the cache: check the warm run answers the same).
subject: SILENT WRONG: in a STRING EVAL, `my $x = $x + 1` where `$x` is a lexical of the enclosing scope reads the NEW (undef) variable in its initialiser -- `my $x = 7; eval q{my $x = $x + 1; $x}` answers 1 (perl 8)
